Counting sign-ins (metrics)#

This page is for the opt-in sign-in counter: what it counts, how to turn it on in a Laravel or raw PHP app, and the queries worth keeping. Read HELMET's metrics guide first: SESAME writes the counter, HELMET serves it.

What it counts#

One counter, sesame_logins_total, with two labels and nothing else:

Label Values
driver cas, fake, gateway, oauth2, oidc, saml, else other
outcome success, failed, refused, unavailable, else other
Outcome When The log event next to it
success The identity was verified and the app's resolver returned a user. sesame.login
failed The driver refused the sign-in: a bad ticket, token or assertion. sesame.login_failed
refused The identity was verified, but the resolver returned null (the app said no). sesame.login_refused
unavailable The identity provider could not be reached, timed out or answered with a 5xx (ProviderUnavailable). sesame.login_failed

A trip to the identity provider is not counted: only the sign-ins that finish. No label ever carries a username, an IP, a session ID or a URL, and both labels are checked against the lists above before they reach the store, so the counter has at most 35 series no matter what the internet sends.

unavailable is the one to alert on: a jump in it means CAS (or Entra, or the IdP) is down for this app, not that people typed the wrong password.

How it reaches /metrics#

SESAME serves no endpoint, holds no token and adds no route. It writes the counter into a promphp store, and HELMET's /metrics renders every metric family in its store. So when SESAME writes to the store HELMET's request metrics use (APCu, Redis or SQLite), the counter shows up on the scrape next to helmet_http_request_duration_seconds, behind HELMET's bearer token or allow list. One endpoint per app, one place to gate it.

PHP shares nothing between requests, so a counter needs a store every worker can reach: that is why the counter needs HELMET's request metrics on (HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE set), not just its endpoint.

Turn it on#

Laravel#

Turn on HELMET's metrics with a store, then SESAME's counter:

HELMET_METRICS_ENABLED=true
HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN=<a long random string, from your secret store>
HELMET_METRICS_STORAGE=apcu
SESAME_METRICS_ENABLED=true

The adapter counts into the app's Prometheus\Storage\Adapter binding when there is one (bind it to share another promphp store), else into the store HELMET's helmet.metrics config names. The store is opened on the first sign-in of a request, never on a request that signs nobody in.

Raw PHP#

Give the facade a PrometheusLoginMetrics as its seventh argument, on HELMET's store:

use Waynestate\Helmet\Metrics\MetricsStorage;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Metrics\PrometheusLoginMetrics;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Sesame;

use function Waynestate\Helmet\helmet_metrics_env;
use function Waynestate\Sesame\sesame;

$helmet = helmet_metrics_env(); // HELMET_METRICS_* and HELMET_POLICY_PATH

$metrics = new PrometheusLoginMetrics(static fn () => MetricsStorage::create(
    $helmet['storage'] ?? null,
    $helmet['redis_url'] ?? null,
    $helmet['sqlite_path'] ?? null,
));

sesame(new Sesame($driver, $resolver, $session, $config, null, $logger, $metrics));

The factory runs on the first sign-in only. Any Prometheus\Storage\Adapter works in its place, if the app keeps its own promphp store. A Wayne Auth app passes the same object as the last argument of WayneAuth::boot().

Check it#

Sign in once, then scrape:

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $HELMET_METRICS_TOKEN" https://your-app.example.test/metrics | grep sesame_

Expect sesame_logins_total{driver="cas",outcome="success"} 1. Nothing there? Look in the log for sesame.metrics_failed (see Troubleshooting).

Graph it in Grafana#

The sign-ins dashboard ships in docs/grafana/sesame.json. In Grafana, open Dashboards, New, Import, upload the file, and pick your Prometheus data source for the DS_PROMETHEUS input. It sits next to HELMET's fleet dashboard and has two rows:

  • Sign-ins: sign-ins in the time range, the success rate, how many hit an unreachable identity provider (red above zero), how many the app refused, and sign-ins per minute by outcome and by driver.
  • When it goes wrong: identity provider outages by app (one app alone points at its own network or HTTP client, every app at once points at the provider), the failed share by driver (a jump after a deploy is usually a changed URL, audience or key), and a table of sign-ins by app, driver and outcome.

job and instance variables at the top narrow every panel. The dashboard was checked against a local Prometheus and Grafana with two simulated apps (one cas, one saml with an identity provider outage) signing in through SESAME into HELMET's SQLite store and scraped from HELMET's /metrics.

Queries worth keeping#

# Sign-ins per minute, by outcome
sum by (outcome) (rate(sesame_logins_total[5m])) * 60

# Share of sign-ins that hit an unreachable identity provider, per app
sum by (instance) (rate(sesame_logins_total{outcome="unavailable"}[5m]))
  / sum by (instance) (rate(sesame_logins_total[5m]))

Counters that reset on a restart are fine: rate() and increase() handle resets. WSU has no Prometheus server yet, so this graphs as soon as one exists and scrapes HELMET's /metrics.

When the store breaks#

Counting is best effort. A store that is down, or a counter turned on with no store to write to, never changes a sign-in: the user is signed in (or refused) exactly as before, and the first count that fails logs one sesame.metrics_failed warning with event, driver and at. The store's own error is never logged, because it can carry a Redis URL with its password; when the cause is SESAME's own setup (no store, promphp not installed), the record adds reason saying what to turn on.
